## Import Data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2026, week = 40)

avocado_oil_bottles <- tuesdata$avocado_oil_bottles
avocado_oil_processed_foods <- tuesdata$avocado_oil_processed_foods
```

## Research Question
Are more expensive bottled avocado oils more likely to have better purity results?

## Data Wrangling
```{r}
avocado_clean <- avocado_oil_bottles %>%
# only keeps related data
  select(
    sample_code,
    grade_labeled,
    product_origin,
    cost_per_fl_oz,
    oxidized,
    purity_result,
    adulterant
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(cost_per_fl_oz),
    !is.na(purity_result)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    purity_result = str_to_title(purity_result),
    oxidation_status = if_else(
      oxidized,
      "Oxidized",
      "Not oxidized"
    ),
    price_group = case_when(
      cost_per_fl_oz < 1.5 ~ "Low price",
      cost_per_fl_oz < 2.5 ~ "Medium price",
      TRUE ~ "High price"
    ),
    price_group = factor(
      price_group,
      levels = c("Low price", "Medium price", "High price")
    )
  )
```

## Plot 1
Does Price Differ by Purity?
```{r}
ggplot(avocado_clean,
       aes(x = purity_result, y = cost_per_fl_oz)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "How Does Price Differ Across Avocado Oil Purity Results?",
    subtitle = paste0(
    "Pure oils tend to have higher prices, but 4 low-price outliers show that\n",
      "pure oils can still be found at very low prices"),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Purity Result",
    caption = paste0(
      "By: Doreen Li, Created on: 10/13/2026, Source: TidyTuesday Avocado Oil\n",
      "Purity results grouped as Adulterated, Pure, or Suspected based on laboratory testing.\n",
    "Each point represents one bottled avocado oil sample."
    )
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 9,
      hjust = 0,
      color = "#7F7F7F"
    )
  )
```

## Conclusion

Higher prices do not indicate better purity in bottled avocado oil. Although pure oils included the most expensive samples, they also spanned the widest price range and included some of the least expensive oils. Meanwhile, adulterated and suspected oils were concentrated at lower prices. Overall, price alone does not appear to be a reliable indicator of purity. Because the dataset contains only 22 samples, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory rather than representative of all bottled avocado oils.
